claims.text: The starting material is cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a single-phase, likely BCC microstructure.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Untreated cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen resistance and oxidizes rapidly under high-temperature oxidizing conditions.
The proposed intervention is deposition of a thin, adherent aluminide coating by pack cementation or vapor deposition.
At high temperature, the aluminide coating will react with oxygen to form an alumina scale.
The resulting Al2O3 scale will be dense, continuous, and adherent.
The alumina scale will act as a barrier to oxygen diffusion.
The alumina barrier will prevent rapid oxygen ingress and oxidation of the HfNbTaTiZr substrate.
After exposure at approximately 1000 °C in air for up to about 100 hours, coated specimens will have lower oxidation weight gain than uncoated controls.
After the specified exposure, coated specimens will have thinner and more adherent oxide scales than uncoated controls.
The coating will preserve high-temperature yield strength at strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1 relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The coating will preserve ductility relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr.
Exposure longer than about 100 hours or at significantly higher temperatures may degrade coating integrity or alter the substrate microstructure.
